About the Role

The company is looking for a Sr. Data Analyst to lead analytics and research into AI search visibility, source citations, content performance, and the relationship between AI-generated recommendations and measurable business results. Reporting to the Vice President of Product, you will help establish reliable methods for measuring how often clients appear in AI answers, how they compare with competitors, and what factors influence those results.

This role combines data analytics, research, experimentation, and LLM evaluation. You will work with structured and unstructured data, develop measurement frameworks, evaluate AI search systems, and collaborate with product and engineering teams to define meaningful metrics. The focus is on producing reliable, transparent findings that help clients understand their performance and identify areas for improvement.

Key Responsibilities

Track how frequently, favorably, and accurately clients appear in AI-generated answers compared with defined competitors, using rigorous baselines, sampling methods, and documented uncertainty.
Maintain tracked-prompt panels across AI engines, topics, and markets, and report changes in visibility over time.
Identify and analyze the sources cited by AI systems for specific topics, including the composition of those sources.
Measure how published content becomes cited evidence in AI answers, how long it takes to appear, and how long citations persist.
Identify gaps in clients' evidence bases and determine what content or sources may be missing.
Test how content characteristics, including source, framing, format, specificity, recency, and structure, affect the likelihood of being cited by AI systems.
Connect AI visibility metrics with referral traffic, engagement, bookings, and conversions, identifying what can be measured reliably and where the connection between recommendations and revenue breaks down.
Evaluate AI-generated answers for accuracy, relevance, and completeness, documenting recurring failure modes across engines.
Maintain evaluation rubrics, benchmarks, and processes for measuring agreement between raters.
Refine prompt construction methods and apply consistent evaluation standards to internally developed AI features.
Research how AI search systems retrieve and cite sources, validating findings through research rather than relying on industry commentary.
Work with product and engineering teams to define product metrics and ensure every customer-facing figure can be reproduced from documented inputs.

5+ years of experience in analytics, data science, research, and/or search products.

Strong SQL and Python skills.
Experience designing experiments using observational data, including comparison group construction, difference-in-differences or matched comparisons, and appropriate consideration of statistical power.

Experience with Databricks or similar data processing and analytics tools is preferred.

The compensation package includes a base salary of $120,000–$140,000, plus equity and an annual bonus.

You will develop performance frameworks that merge operational SLAs (e.g., on-time arrival, inbox turnaround times) with clinical quality and safety metrics. Your Impact at LILA

Lila’s mission is to accelerate scientific discovery with AI, and that depends on trustworthy scientific data. As a Data Engineer, you’ll build ETL pipelines and data models for Lila’s scientific data platform, working at the intersection of data engineering, computational biology, chemistry, and materials science.

You’ll partner with AI researchers and experimentalists to turn raw lab instrument outputs into validated, analysis-ready datasets. The core challenge is data modeling: transforming messy, per-instrument measurements into clean, well-typed data that is efficient to query, reliable to use, and ready for downstream analysis.

You’ll also build domain-specific analysis functions and reusable data pipelines that help scientists and AI researchers move faster without re-deriving bespoke solutions.

What You'll Be Building

Design pipelines that turn raw lab output into analysis-ready scientific data.
Model heterogeneous data from bio, chemistry, and materials instruments.
Build validation checks, schema-evolution gates, and data quality workflows.
Develop reusable analysis functions for scientific and AI research workflows.
Improve automation and observability across instrument-to-result data flows.
Build canonical datasets that scientists and AI researchers can trust.
Use AI coding tools to accelerate pipeline development and team velocity.

What You'll Need To Succeed

2–6 years of experience in data engineering, bioinformatics, cheminformatics, or computational science. Strong Python skills, including typed, tested, production-quality code.
Strong SQL skills, especially with Postgres or similar relational databases.
Experience building ETL pipelines, data models, and reusable data transformations.
Data science foundation, including statistics and pandas, NumPy, or similar tools.
Experience translating noisy scientific measurements into accurate, validated datasets.
Workflow orchestration experience, ideally Flyte, Airflow, Prefect, Dagster, or Nextflow.
Active use of AI coding tools in day-to-day engineering work.

Familiarity with event-driven pipelines such as NATS or Kafka.

Familiarity with life sciences assays, sequencing, imaging, or flow cytometry.
